segments.text: Before 1956, moving cargo across an ocean was slow, manual work.
Goods went aboard piece by piece, and ships sat in port for days.
On April 26, 1956, the Ideal X sailed from Newark with 58 metal containers.
Standard sizes followed: twenty or forty feet, stackable on any ship, train, or truck.
Loading cost fell from about six dollars a ton to sixteen cents.
Economists find containers lifted trade more than trade agreements did.
One steel box made the world smaller.
